articles.headline: Two CJP leaders sent to jail over Jantar Mantar stir
articles.blurb: Cockroach Janta Party co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were remanded to five-day judicial custody over the Jantar Mantar protest.

articles.headline: 2 detained, let off in 'fake' Siddu video case
articles.blurb: Two people detained in connection with an allegedly fake video targeting Chief Minister Siddaramaiah were questioned and let off.

articles.headline: Retail rush: Festive purse opens for clothes, gifts and holidays
articles.blurb: Bengaluru households are prioritising clothing, festive gifting and travel as seasonal shopping picks up, with retailers reporting stronger interest in apparel, smartphones, laptops and home appliances. A LocalCircles survey of Bengaluru consumers found 52% plan to spend on clothing, footwear and accessories; among spending-plan respondents, 23% expected to spend Rs 10,001–25,000.

articles.headline: Realtor killed as SUV rams into LPG cylinder lorry
articles.blurb: Thirty-six-year-old realtor Shivakumar M of Madanahatti in Malur taluk, Kolar, was killed and four others injured when their Range Rover rammed into a stationary LPG-cylinder lorry on NH-648 near Devanahalli on Tuesday evening. Devanahalli Traffic Police registered a negligence case; both the Range Rover driver Pavan and the lorry driver fled the scene.

articles.headline: KRV seeks ban on Sonu Nigam's concert in city
articles.blurb: Karnataka Rakshana Vedike urged Bengaluru City Police to deny permission for singer Sonu Nigam to perform in the city, accusing him of insulting Kannadigas by linking demands for Kannada songs to the Pahalgam terror attack. KRV state president T A Narayanagowda cited remarks from an April 2025 Bengaluru concert in a letter dated October 14.

articles.headline: Rahul's Gen-Z moment as Cong reaches out to CJP
articles.blurb: Analysis by Shemin Joy (Thaw, finally) says the jailing of Cockroach Janta Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka over their tricolour protest at Jantar Mantar opened the door for Congress–CJP engagement after mutual suspicion. Rahul Gandhi signalled unity behind one protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and sought to bring Gen-Z activists into a wider movement.

articles.headline: Leader of Opposition warns against violence on students
articles.blurb: Rahul Gandhi met NSUI members and other protesters who said they were injured in police action during protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, and warned against violence on students. He highlighted Athira, a Kerala student and NSUI member who is visually impaired and hard of hearing.

articles.headline: BJP mocks Oppn over errors in petition against CEC
articles.blurb: The BJP said the Opposition's Supreme Court petition against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had multiple deficiencies, claiming affidavits of nine leaders were missing and listing 14 mistakes in all. It said the Opposition's election preparations were in the same vein as 'vote theft' charges.

articles.headline: FIR against women journalists
articles.blurb: Delhi Police registered an FIR against an independent journalist and others after a complaint by one of its officers alleging casteist remarks, public humiliation and defamation during a protest near Jantar Mantar earlier this month.

articles.headline: Dhruv Rathee summoned
articles.blurb: A Delhi court summoned YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in a 2018 defamation case, noting he has been living in Austria for the past seven years and has not come to India for the proceedings.

articles.headline: DMK legal aid to detainees
articles.blurb: Strongly condemning the jailing of CJP leaders and related crackdowns, DMK said it would extend legal aid to detainees linked to the protests.

articles.headline: Keralam exam question
articles.blurb: A Kerala PSC examination question referring to the Jantar Mantar agitations sparked controversy.

articles.headline: Portal for info on demographic change launched
articles.blurb: A portal for information on demographic change was launched in New Delhi.

articles.headline: Ex-Thane mayor to be questioned
articles.blurb: An SIT is to question former Thane mayor Mayur Meenakshi Shinde in connection with the murder of Santosh Punnekar.

articles.headline: Allahabad HC on 'dummy school'
articles.blurb: The Allahabad High Court directed an inquiry into 'dummy schools' in Uttar Pradesh.

articles.headline: Bihar capsize: 6 rescued
articles.blurb: Six people were rescued after a boat capsized in the Ganga in Vaishali district, Bihar.

articles.headline: Rahul, Priyanka protest with U'khand murder victim's family over Sikkim Guv appointment
articles.blurb: Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra joined the parents of murdered hotel receptionist Ankita Bhandari in an India Gate protest against the appointment of BJP leader Dushyant Kumar Gautam as Sikkim Governor. The family said it saw no progress despite the Uttarakhand BJP-led government handing the case to the CBI.

articles.headline: SC orders insurance cover for all counter-bought rly tickets
articles.blurb: The Supreme Court directed Indian Railways to extend insurance cover to all tickets purchased over the counter at railway stations from October 27, warning the Railway Board would be held directly responsible for any failure to implement the order.

articles.headline: SP rebel MLAs join BJP at Amethi event
articles.blurb: Three rebel Samajwadi Party MLAs — Rakesh Pratap Singh, Abhai Singh and Vinod Chaturvedi — who had defied the party whip joined the BJP at an Amethi event.

articles.headline: Keralam's paddy guardian leaves behind a rich seed bank
articles.blurb: A tribute notes that Padma Shri Cheruvayal Raman, a Wayanad tribal farmer known for conserving traditional paddy, left behind a rich seed bank of indigenous rice varieties.

articles.headline: Jio to launch India IPO on October 21
articles.blurb: Jio Platforms Limited filed its red herring prospectus for an initial public offering; the offer opens for subscription on October 21 and closes on October 23, with listing expected around October 28.

articles.headline: Congress Manipur MP summoned over JNU sexual harassment case
articles.blurb: Delhi Police summoned Congress Lok Sabha MP from Manipur Inner, Bimol Akoijam, for questioning over an FIR of sexual harassment lodged by a group of students at Jawaharlal Nehru University. His supporters protested outside the BJP state office in Imphal; ABVP also staged a protest seeking his arrest.

articles.headline: 2 top CJP leaders jailed over Jantar Mantar stir
articles.blurb: Cockroach Janta Party co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, detained after a flash protest against the Chief Election Commissioner at Jantar Mantar, were sent to five-day judicial custody and lodged in Tihar Jail. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and others voiced support; CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke announced a 'Jabra Tiranga' tricolour stir at Connaught Place's Central Park on Friday.

articles.headline: Two suspects grilled & let off in 'doctored' Siddu video case
articles.blurb: Bengaluru police detained, questioned and later let off two suspects, including a YouTube content creator, over circulation of an allegedly doctored video targeting former chief minister Siddaramaiah. Investigators are probing the video's origin, motive and possible conspiracy; Home Minister Priyank Kharge ruled out a CBI probe into sting operations against politicians.

articles.headline: Air India flight diverted after false hijack alert
articles.blurb: Air India flight AI2090 from Frankfurt to Delhi, a Boeing 787-9 with about 230 passengers and crew, was diverted to Jaipur on Wednesday after a hijack alert that later proved false. After security checks at Jaipur International Airport around 9:35 am, the flight received clearance and resumed its journey to Delhi.

articles.headline: Sugarcane farmers continue protest
articles.blurb: Traffic on the Pune–Bengaluru national highway remained affected for a second consecutive day as sugarcane farmers protested unmet demands, with demonstrations at toll plazas including Wirebagewadi in Belagavi. Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha and related farmer groups said protests would continue till the Centre addressed their issues; a padyatra toward Hubballi was also reported.

articles.headline: Tiger, elephant found dead in Bandipur Reserve
articles.blurb: A tiger and an elephant were found dead in Bandipur Tiger Reserve in suspected poaching incidents, forest officials said; the elephant carcass was missing both tusks. Conservator of Forests L Nandish said a special team led by an ACF was probing the cases and that disciplinary action would follow if patrol lapses were found.

articles.headline: 2023 Sringeri poll: SC flays EC over missing counting video
articles.blurb: The Supreme Court pulled up the Election Commission for saying it could not trace the 2023 video recording of vote counting in the Sringeri Assembly constituency. A bench of Justices Sanjiv Khanna and others pressed for observer reports and related records; the Congress legislator's challenge to the recount outcome was posted to February 15, 2027.

articles.headline: Pvt hospitals must display treatment rate card: Khader
articles.blurb: Health Minister U T Khader directed private hospitals to display treatment rate cards within their premises so prices are clearly visible to the public, saying it is mandatory under the Karnataka Private Medical Establishments Act. He also said hospitals should indicate the actual purchase cost of medicines alongside MRP so discounted procurement benefits reach patients.

articles.headline: BJP mocks Oppn over plea errors
articles.blurb: Listing what it called deficiencies in the Opposition's Supreme Court petition against the CEC, the BJP said the Opposition came to bring change but its election preparations were just as flawed as its 'vote theft' claims.

articles.headline: CJP for 'tricolour stir' on Friday
articles.blurb: Strongly opposing the jailing of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, founder Abhijeet Dipke announced a 'Jabra Tiranga' (unfurl the tricolour) gathering at Connaught Place's Central Park on Friday evening.

articles.headline: Protest against Sikkim Guv appointment
articles.blurb: Parents of murdered hotel receptionist Ankita Bhandari staged a protest at India Gate against the appointment of BJP leader Dushyant Kumar Gautam as Sikkim Governor, joined by Congress leaders including Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra.

articles.headline: Iran says ship sank after striking mine
articles.blurb: Iran said a cargo ship sank after hitting a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz, reporting it as the first such sinking after a mine strike during the recent conflict period.

articles.headline: Jaishankar arrives in UAE on 3-day visit
articles.blurb: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar arrived in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday on a three-day visit to the UAE to review progress of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with his Emirati counterpart.

articles.headline: Ukraine accuses US of helping Russia
articles.blurb: Ukraine accused the US of helping Russia, with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also accusing Russia of flouting a supposed 'energy ceasefire' announced by Donald Trump.

articles.headline: SC orders insurance for all counter-bought rly tickets
articles.blurb: The Supreme Court directed Indian Railways to extend insurance cover to all tickets purchased over the counter at railway stations from October 27.

articles.headline: Sexual assault: Cong MP summoned
articles.blurb: Congress Lok Sabha MP from Manipur Inner, Bimol Akoijam, was summoned by Delhi Police for questioning in connection with an FIR alleging sexual harassment lodged by a group of students at Jawaharlal Nehru University.

articles.headline: 'No changes made to crop insurance term sheet, BJP spreading misinformation'
articles.blurb: Dakshina Kannada DCC president Padmaraj R Poojary said BJP leaders were spreading misinformation about the weather-based crop insurance scheme and that the state had made no changes to the term sheet for arecanut and black pepper. He said the total premium rate quoted was 35%, with farmers contributing 5%, the Centre 10% and the state 20%, and outlined rainfall/temperature-linked payout rules including Rs 144 per hectare per mm above a 225 mm rain threshold.

articles.headline: Traffic restrictions in view of CM's visit to Kudroli
articles.blurb: Mangaluru City Police warned of congestion on Thursday evening as Chief Minister D K Shivakumar is scheduled to visit Kudroli Gokarnanatha Temple for Mangaluru Dasara. Traffic between New Chitra Junction and Durgamahal Junction should be avoided from 4 pm to 8 pm; Kudroli main road will not be available for vehicles or parking, and visitors were told to park in the Mannagudda–Gandhinagar area.

articles.headline: 'Climate action is no longer charity; it is engine of green growth'
articles.blurb: EMPRI Bengaluru and NITK Surathkal organised a stakeholders' workshop on blue carbon ecosystems and mangrove carbon-credit projects. Karnataka Net Zero Task Force vice-chairperson Upendra Tripathy and Principal Secretary Srinivasulu stressed partnership-led climate action; Tripathy said the collaboration could aim to cut half a million tonnes of carbon emissions over five years.

articles.headline: 30 vehicles ferrying schoolchildren booked for violating rules
articles.blurb: Mangaluru Regional Transport Office registered cases against around 30 vehicles for illegally transporting schoolchildren during a special inspection drive, and issued notices to owners warning that registrations could be suspended.

articles.headline: BSNL officials told to expedite works on towers
articles.blurb: Udupi-Chikmagalur MP Kota Srinivasa Poojary directed BSNL officials at a progress review to upgrade facilities from 3G to 4G, maintain DG sets and batteries, and expedite new towers on 39 allotted sites. He flagged network problems at the Deputy Commissioner's office in Manipal, nearby hospitals, and tourist spots such as Kaup and Kamalashile.

articles.headline: 3-day meet at MAHE to address critical global health priorities
articles.blurb: Manipal Academy of Higher Education inaugurated a three-day Nature conference on infectious diseases in a changing world, running through October 16 with partners including Nature Medicine and participants from 20 countries. MAHE Vice-Chancellor Dr Sharath K Rao stressed stronger surveillance, preparedness and equitable healthcare access.

articles.headline: Govt invites public suggestions/objections on renaming DK dist as M'luru
articles.blurb: The state government proposed renaming Dakshina Kannada district as Mangaluru district and invited suggestions and objections within 30 days of Gazette publication. Additional Chief Secretary (Revenue) Rajender Kumar Kataria's October 1 notification cited public demand and administrative convenience; representations can go to the CM's Secretariat, Revenue Department, or the DK Deputy Commissioner.

articles.headline: Taxi Men's Assn sets deadline for MIA to withdraw toll fee
articles.blurb: Dakshina Kannada Taxi Men's and Maxicab Association set a 10-day deadline for Mangaluru International Airport to withdraw the Rs 50 toll on commercial vehicles entering airport premises. Honorary president and former MLA K Raghupathi Bhat warned of an indefinite relay hunger strike if the fee is not withdrawn.

articles.headline: Elderly man loses Rs 14.35L to scam
articles.blurb: A 75-year-old Udupi man, Ramesh Shetty, allegedly lost Rs 14,35,724 in an online trading scam after fraudsters shared a Facebook link in the name of HDFC Securities. When he tried to withdraw funds, they demanded a further Rs 5,10,724 and then stopped responding.

articles.headline: 4 held for illegally transporting cattle
articles.blurb: Kota police in Udupi district arrested four men for allegedly illegally transporting eight cows, including calves, in a pickup near Tekkatte on the national highway. Police seized the vehicle valued at about Rs 2 lakh, cattle valued at Rs 29,000, phones and cash.

articles.headline: Applications invited for Yenepoya Teacher Awards
articles.blurb: Yenepoya Moideen Kunhi Memorial Educational & Charitable Trust invited applications for Yenepoya Teacher Awards 2026 across four categories, each with a Rs 25,000 cash prize. Eligible educators need three years' continuous service; last date to apply is October 31, with felicitation on November 14 at Deralakatte.

articles.headline: 9th convocation of Srinivas University today
articles.blurb: Srinivas University will hold its ninth annual convocation on October 15 at its Mukka campus, with 2,077 graduates receiving certificates, including 395 postgraduate and 1,619 undergraduate students, plus 63 research scholars. Sadbhavana Divas marking founder Raghavendra Rao's 90th birth anniversary will be observed on October 16.

articles.headline: Sowjanya case: SIT holds series of meetings
articles.blurb: The Special Investigation Team reconstituted by the state government to reinvestigate the 2012 rape and murder of Sowjanya held a series of meetings in Mangaluru and is verifying case documents. SIT chief N Shashi Kumar said the team is likely to visit Sowjanya's residence in Beltangady shortly.

articles.headline: BDA offers up to Rs 4 lakh for info on encroached properties
articles.blurb: Bangalore Development Authority announced cash rewards of up to Rs 4 lakh for information on its encroached or forged-document-linked properties, with informants' identities to be kept confidential. Rewards include Rs 50,000 for a 20 ft x 30 ft site; Commissioner Major P Manivannan said payouts follow verification as BDA seeks to monetise land assets.

articles.headline: DRDO to focus on next-gen chips at innovation conclave
articles.blurb: DRDO will lead a session on identifying challenges and opportunities in next-generation chips at the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC-2026) in New Delhi from October 27 to 29, with Distinguished Scientist and Director General (Micro Electronic Devices) S K Das among speakers.

articles.headline: Incorrect info given to SC: Alok Kumar in letter to CS
articles.blurb: DGP (Prisons and Correctional Services) Alok Kumar wrote to the chief secretary expressing dissatisfaction that incorrect information was given to the Supreme Court regarding phone-tapping probes. He sought verification of details on an SIT led by him and related B-report claims dating to February 2024.

articles.headline: '108' ambulance crew meet health secretary, return to duty
articles.blurb: Suvarna Karnataka Arogya Kavach (108) ambulance crew returned to duty after meeting the health secretary, though an October 22 protest has not been called off yet. The crew had gone on indefinite strike over unmet demands including salaries and service conditions.

articles.headline: HC slaps Rs 1 lakh on LAO for neglecting 102-yr-old petitioner
articles.blurb: The Karnataka High Court imposed costs of Rs 1 lakh on a Special Land Acquisition Officer for neglecting statutory duties toward a 102-year-old petitioner in a land acquisition matter involving about 29 guntas.

articles.headline: Nine more taluks declared drought-hit; tally rises to 226
articles.blurb: Nine more taluks were declared drought-hit on Wednesday, raising Karnataka's drought-affected tally to 226. The report outlined moderately and severely affected taluks across regions including south interior Karnataka.

articles.headline: RERA orders villa developer to fix defects within 90 days
articles.blurb: Karnataka RERA directed the developer of a Bengaluru villa project to rectify construction defects and deviations within 90 days, after allottees complained about quality and related issues.

articles.headline: VB-G RAM G: Record 2.04 cr persondays of jobs generated
articles.blurb: Karnataka generated a record 2.04 crore persondays of jobs under the VB-G RAM G rural employment scheme, with district-wise figures including strong generation in Bidar and Kalaburagi among others.

articles.headline: Jamaat-e-Islami flags 'threats' to electoral integrity, right to protest
articles.blurb: Jamaat-e-Islami Hind expressed concern over threats to electoral integrity and the right to protest, citing issues around the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and police action against protesters.

articles.headline: Widespread rain across K'taka from today: IMD
articles.blurb: IMD forecast widespread rain/thundershowers across Karnataka from Thursday, covering interior north, coastal and south interior districts including Bengaluru Urban.

articles.headline: 2 Gescom engineers land in Lokayukta trap
articles.blurb: Lokayukta police in Yadgir trapped two junior Gescom engineers who were allegedly accepting a bribe to clear a work-related file.

articles.headline: Dengue prevention should be a year-round initiative: Experts
articles.blurb: Experts at a Bengaluru workshop urged shifting dengue control from seasonal measures to year-round preparedness, citing climate change and the need for surveillance, community prevention and rapid diagnosis. Health Minister U T Khader and other stakeholders backed stronger public-health coordination.

articles.headline: Rivals turn 'allies' for Siddu in 'sting op' war
articles.blurb: BJP and JD(S) leaders publicly backed former chief minister Siddaramaiah amid a controversial sting-operation video, with analysts saying the Opposition senses an 'inside job' aimed at cornering Deputy CM D K Shivakumar. BJP state president B Y Vijayendra claimed attempts within Congress to politically sideline Siddaramaiah.

articles.headline: Ramesh Jarkiholi calls on Siddaramaiah
articles.blurb: BJP leader Ramesh Jarkiholi met Siddaramaiah in Bengaluru and said he remains 'our leader' regardless of party, urging him not to seek a court stay over sting-operation allegations. Minister P M Narendraswamy also visited the former CM; Yathindra Siddaramaiah alleged a conspiracy to tarnish his father's image.

articles.headline: PM Modi appreciates VIT Chennai-incubated MEDxAI Innovations' healthcare technologies
articles.blurb: Prime Minister Narendra Modi appreciated AI-based healthcare technologies of MEDxAI Innovations Pvt Ltd, a deep-tech startup incubated at VIT Chennai, during inauguration of the Porur Metro Rail project. Founded by VIT faculty Dr Sheena C Pravin and Dr Reena Monica P, the firm showcased tools including Cervilens cervical-cancer pre-screening and Quantum PharmX drug-discovery platforms.

articles.headline: BYV's claim of Cong exodus revives 'insider-outsider' debate
articles.blurb: BJP state president B Y Vijayendra's claim that about 25 Congress leaders would jump ship before the 2028 elections revived debate over inducting outsiders versus long-time BJP workers. The report recalled Operation Kamala-style defections and disgruntlement among several BJP leaders.

articles.headline: 'Captain cool' Prashantha is howdah elephant this Dasara
articles.blurb: Fifty-four-year-old elephant Prashantha has been finalised to carry the golden howdah seating Goddess Chamundeshwari in Mysuru Dasara's Jamboo Savari, succeeding Abhimanyu who turned 60. Forest officials cited his calm temperament, load-bearing capacity and training with a 700-kg sand bag; Dhananjaya is the reserve howdah elephant.

articles.headline: Cong launches 2nd phase of campaign to build party
articles.blurb: Karnataka Congress launched the second phase of its Sanghatana Srujan Abhiyan in Bengaluru South to strengthen grassroots organisation ahead of local body polls, with KPCC leaders stressing women's participation and review of long-serving office-bearers.

articles.headline: Half-burnt voter ID cards found by roadside
articles.blurb: Hundreds of half-burnt voter ID cards, Aadhaar and PAN documents belonging to people from Hassan, Bengaluru, Ramanagara and other places were found by the roadside in Sakleshpur town. Town police said the cards appeared discarded after accumulating with a hotel or similar premises and that a video was circulating on social media.

articles.headline: Govt to celebrate Madhwacharya Jayanti
articles.blurb: Kannada and Culture Minister Shivaraj Tangadagi said the state government will observe Madhwacharya Jayanti as a state-level function every year on October 21, with a government order issued in that regard.

articles.headline: SC reserves verdict on K'taka law validating 2011 KPSC recruitments
articles.blurb: The Supreme Court reserved judgment on a petition challenging a Karnataka High Court order that upheld the Karnataka Civil Services (Validation of Selection and Appointment of 2011 Gazetted Probationers) Act, 2022, covering 362 KPSC-selected candidates. A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Vinod Chandran directed detailed affidavits by October 26, noting the original 2011 process was marred by irregularities.

articles.headline: Central panel to address sugarcane farmers' concerns
articles.blurb: The Centre constituted a committee chaired by former NITI Aayog member Ramesh Chand to examine issues raised by sugarcane farmers, particularly from Karnataka and Maharashtra, and recommend measures. The move follows an October 2 meeting of Union ministers with about 80–90 farmers; the panel will review remunerative returns, MSP of sugar and related mill practices.

articles.headline: 2 detained, grilled & let off in 'doctored' Siddu video case
articles.blurb: Continuing the Siddu video probe, Home Minister Priyank Kharge said Karnataka Police were equipped to handle the case and ruled out a CBI probe, while slamming JD(S) claims that Congress leaders were out to destroy Siddaramaiah. HD Kumaraswamy accused the government of targeting JD(S) social media workers, citing detention of worker Shankar after a complaint over alleged honey-trap videos.

articles.headline: RTE expenditure: Schools' body moves HC for national criteria
articles.blurb: The Karnataka High Court ordered notice to the Union and state governments on a petition by associated managements of government-recognised English-medium schools seeking national criteria for fixing per-child expenditure under the RTE Act. Petitioners said the state has continued a 2017 PCE notification without updating it for 2026–27, forcing unaided schools to bear unreimbursed 25% quota costs.

articles.headline: Schools' assn seeks law to protect teachers, kids, schools
articles.blurb: Associated managements of primary and secondary schools in Karnataka demanded a Karnataka Education Safety, Institutional Security and Teacher Protection Bill after alleged assaults and intimidation of teachers and institutions. The association told CM D K Shivakumar such incidents create fear, disturb the academic atmosphere and undermine the dignity of the teaching profession.

articles.headline: Quota enhancement: Reform without rigour (Opinion)
articles.blurb: An editorial says the Karnataka High Court judgment striking down the law raising SC reservation from 15% to 17% and ST reservation from 3% to 7% underscores the peril of legislating without a firm constitutional foundation. The bench held the hike breached the 50% ceiling without extraordinary circumstances or rigorous assessment, and faulted the government for not consulting national SC/ST commissions.

articles.headline: Longer lives, with some red flags (Opinion)
articles.blurb: An editorial on WHO Global Health Estimates notes global life expectancy recovered to about 73.3 years in 2023 and India's to 71 years, while warning that healthy life expectancy lags and non-communicable diseases remain a major threat. It argues India must invest more in public health so added years are lived in good health.

articles.headline: CJP's challenge is to be differently different (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Valson Thampu and Debasish Bhattacharyya argue Cockroach Janta Party's credibility depends on resisting political opportunism and partisan capture while translating protest momentum into durable change. They urge CJP to maintain independence from established parties, avoid Trojan-horse appropriation, and keep purpose over transactional politics.

articles.headline: The wedding crasher (Opinion)
articles.blurb: In a Right in the Middle column, Shilpa Bhat recounts accidentally gate-crashing the wrong Bengaluru wedding reception while hunting for a colleague's function, before finding the correct hall and dinner.

articles.headline: Why the EU may want Britain back (Opinion)
articles.blurb: K M Rakesh writes that shifting geopolitics — including the Ukraine war, US uncertainty and investment needs — may make the EU more open to a UK return, while noting sticking points on people, goods, services, capital and the euro.

articles.headline: Amit Shah has missed the point (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Letter writer T P Pandarinath Naidu of Hubballi criticises Union Home Minister Amit Shah for focusing on 2029 polls instead of addressing SIR-related protests, alleged disenfranchisement and police excesses against students and CJP demonstrators.

articles.headline: Ambulance strike (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Shishir Patil of Bengaluru writes that the 108 ambulance technicians' strike reflects unmet demands after failed talks and warns that interrupting emergency services highlights official apathy.

articles.headline: Karnataka HC is right (Opinion)
articles.blurb: K R Jayaprakash Rao of Mysuru supports the High Court striking down the SC/ST quota hike, saying the state government's proposal violated the Supreme Court's 50% reservation norm.

articles.headline: The politics of pandal in the battle to reshape West Bengal's cultural ethos
articles.blurb: Anirban Bhaumik reports how Durga Puja pandals in Kolkata have become a political arena as BJP and TMC compete through themes, patronage and cultural messaging. The feature tracks festival economics, Hindutva outreach and counter-assertions of Bengali cultural identity during the annual festivities.

articles.headline: A movie on a political killing fuels South Korea's culture wars
articles.blurb: Choe Sang-Hun reports that the film The Assassin(s) revisits the 1974 shooting that killed Yuk Young-soo, wife of South Korean dictator Park Chung-hee, and has reignited polarized debates and conspiracy theories over the country's modern history.

articles.headline: A tale of two protests (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Arvind Narrain compares the right to protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi with protest restrictions in Bengaluru, including Freedom Park rules and police permission battles, arguing democratic space depends on protecting peaceful assembly.

articles.headline: Before you pour (Opinion)
articles.blurb: In the Oasis column, Aditi Pant reflects on a young girl's compassion for a hungry stray dog and a lesson in generosity before sharing food and drink.

articles.headline: Houthis vow more attacks after hitting Saudi oil giant
articles.blurb: Yemen's Houthis claimed a strike on a building in Saudi Aramco's Dhahran operations centre and vowed further attacks; Saudi officials reported damage to upper floors of an executive building with no casualties. A Saudi-led coalition said intercepted missiles and drones left debris that injured four people and damaged about 15 houses in Riyadh.

articles.headline: UK university offers for foreign students hit by study visa refusals
articles.blurb: UK universities are withdrawing offers to international students amid a surge in study-visa refusals under tougher Home Office rules, with Financial Times analysis of official data pointing to especially high refusal rates for applicants from countries including Pakistan and Nigeria.

articles.headline: Iran sinks cargo ship
articles.blurb: Iran said a cargo ship sank after striking a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz, describing it as the first such mine-related sinking since the end of the tanker war period.

articles.headline: Trump's new press secretary faces scrutiny over credentials
articles.blurb: White House press secretary Karie Zacharia faced scrutiny after questions about whether she passed the California bar exam; the State Bar of California was asked to investigate aspects of her legal credentials.

articles.headline: Trump cuts refugees' deadline to challenge status revocation
articles.blurb: The Trump administration reduced the time refugees have to challenge revocation of their status from 30 days to 10 days, according to a Miami-datelined report.

articles.headline: Rubio to visit India on Oct 17
articles.blurb: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is scheduled to visit India, including New Delhi and Jamnagar, around October 17 in connection with Quad foreign ministers' engagement and bilateral talks.

articles.headline: Ukraine accuses US of helping Russia as missiles hit Kyiv
articles.blurb: As missiles hit Kyiv, Ukraine accused the US of helping Russia, with aides linking Starlink restrictions to the political situation under the new US administration.

articles.headline: France opens probe against 14-yr-old over school shooting
articles.blurb: French authorities opened a probe against a 14-year-old over a premeditated school shooting at Lakanal middle school in Aubagne, near Marseille.

articles.headline: Police confiscate robot that groped teen girl
articles.blurb: German police in Cologne confiscated a remote-controlled robot allegedly used to harass a 16-year-old girl.

articles.headline: Actor Russell Brand is a sexual predator, says prosecutor
articles.blurb: A London prosecutor told Southwark Crown Court that actor Russell Brand is a sexual predator as he faces charges involving multiple women; Brand has pleaded not guilty.

articles.headline: 3 Indians die in Germany fire
articles.blurb: Three Indian nationals died in a residential building fire in Bochum, Germany; a 41-year-old Romanian national was detained in connection with the blaze.

articles.headline: Gunman kills 4 in South Africa
articles.blurb: A gunman killed four people at a memorial service in Johannesburg, South Africa.

articles.headline: Pope undergoes cancer surgery
articles.blurb: Pope Leo XIV underwent surgery for colon cancer at Gemelli hospital in Rome.

articles.headline: Windies' Hope comes to fruition
articles.blurb: Captain Shai Hope's unbeaten 102 and Keemo Paul's five for 41 helped West Indies beat India by 24 runs in the fourth T20I at Hyderabad, levelling the five-match series 2-2. India fell short chasing 247 despite contributions including Sanju Samson's 56; the fifth T20I is at Bengaluru's M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Saturday.

articles.headline: Gritty Andhra thwart Karnataka's late charge
articles.blurb: In the Ranji Trophy at Alur, Andhra held on for a draw despite Karun Nair's unbeaten 155 for Karnataka, with Andhra taking three points on first-innings lead.

articles.headline: Santner bats for balanced surfaces for limited-overs leg
articles.blurb: New Zealand's Mitchell Santner, speaking ahead of the limited-overs series against India, said he wants balanced surfaces rather than extremes for the white-ball leg.

articles.headline: MLAs to get two complimentary tickets for Bengaluru T20I
articles.blurb: Each Karnataka MLA will receive two complimentary tickets for the India–West Indies T20I at M Chinnaswamy Stadium, with digital tickets to be issued via the Speaker's office; a special stand has been reserved for legislators.

articles.headline: Satwik-Chirag crash out on bad day for Indians
articles.blurb: Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty crashed out of the Denmark Open in the round of 32, while other Indians including Ayush Shetty and Unnati Hooda also exited on a difficult opening day in Odense.

articles.headline: BFI president, secretary general suspend each other
articles.blurb: Boxing Federation of India president Ajay Singh and secretary general Hemanta Kumar Kalita suspended each other amid a leadership conflict in the federation.

articles.headline: Bouli hands Punjab the win
articles.blurb: Punjab FC beat Odisha FC 2-1 in the Indian Super League, with Bouli proving decisive in the win.

articles.headline: Indian boxers to compete in U-19 Worlds
articles.blurb: An 11-member Indian boxing team will compete at the Under-19 World Championships in Montenegro.
